seo.title: Central America Semester Abroad | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Mexico, Belize, Guatemala & Costa Rica in 10 weeks: Chichén Itzá, PADI certification, the ATM Cave, an Acatenango volcano hike, Spanish homestays and Pacuare rafting. Ages 17–22.

phases.text: Belize · PADI certification and marine conservation with Blue Ventures, a sailing trip to Caye Caulker’s islands, Lower Dover Lodge and the ATM Cave

items.body: Clean, comfortable stays such as Chill Inn Hostel in Tulum, Sandbar Hostel in Belize, Lower Dover Lodge, Tortuguero Lodge and a river lodge on the Pacuare.

items.title: Host families
items.body: Homestays with local families while you study Spanish in Tulum and in Quetzaltenango (Xela).

items.title: Camping & retreats

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Tulum, cenotes & Chichén Itzá
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors at Cancun airport and transfer to Tulum for orientation. We explore the cliff-top Tulum ruins, swim in Cenote Dos Ojos and head inland to Chichén Itzá.

Then you move in with a host family and start Spanish lessons at Meztli Spanish School. Afternoons bring arts and crafts and salsa dance lessons, and we spend a morning in the Sian Ka’an biosphere reserve.

weeks.title: Spanish study & journey to Belize
weeks.body:
Spanish lessons continue alongside yoga, a Mexican cooking class and a meet-up with locals for an English/Spanish language exchange, with a day to rest and time by the sea between lessons.

Midweek we travel south via Chetumal and take the ferry to San Pedro, Belize, where we settle in at the Blue Ventures dive camp and begin PADI dive training.

weeks.title: Diving & marine conservation
weeks.body:
Life on the Caribbean Sea becomes our classroom. We keep working through PADI certification with Blue Ventures, developing underwater skills while learning about marine ecosystems. Days are filled with pool sessions, open water dives and environmental education.

After a rest day and a resupply run in San Pedro, we join Blue Ventures for three days of marine conservation service learning, contributing to hands-on conservation efforts.
weeks.imageAlt: Two scuba divers silhouetted against sunlight underwater

weeks.title: Island hopping, jungle & the ATM Cave
weeks.location: San Pedro → Caye Caulker → Lower Dover Lodge, Belize
weeks.body:
A public boat takes us to Caye Caulker, then we set off on a two-day sailing trip with Raggamuffin Tours, island hopping, snorkeling and camping on an island.

From Dangriga we transfer inland to Lower Dover Lodge to explore its trails and ruins and swim. A highlight of the week is the ATM Cave expedition, combining physical adventure with cultural history.

weeks.title: Tikal, Antigua & Acatenango
weeks.body:
We visit the Belize Zoo, then cross into Guatemala and stay at Jungle Lodge Tikal. Next we fly on and transfer to Antigua, a colonial city surrounded by volcanoes, for a day tour of San Juan del Obispo.

Then comes a multi-day hike on Acatenango volcano, camping under the stars and supporting one another as a team, before a rest day back in Antigua.
weeks.imageAlt: Group of students in warm jackets on a mountainside with a smoking volcano behind

weeks.title: Coffee culture & a Xela homestay
weeks.body:
We join the De la Gente Bike Coffee Tour in Antigua to learn about sustainable farming and local livelihoods.

Then we travel to Quetzaltenango (Xela) to meet our host families and study Spanish at Sisai Language School for five days, practicing in real-world contexts. Living alongside local families gives insight into daily life. At the end of the week we set off on a hike to Lake Atitlán.
weeks.imageAlt: Group of students standing together above the clouds at sunrise

weeks.title: Lake Atitlán & a yoga retreat
weeks.location: Lake Atitlán, Guatemala → San José, Costa Rica
weeks.body:
Our multi-day hike continues to Lake Atitlán, camping along the way. We then slow the pace at the Doron Yoga & Zen Center, with morning yoga and meditation sessions and afternoon Spanish lessons.

A boat to Panajachel starts our journey to Guatemala City, where we spend a night before flying to San José, Costa Rica, and transferring to Rancho Tinamu.
weeks.imageAlt: Students on yoga mats in a bamboo hall with a lake and mountains outside

weeks.title: Farm service & a kayaking expedition
weeks.location: San Isidro de Dota → Puntarenas, Costa Rica
weeks.body:
At Rancho Tinamu in San Isidro de Dota we spend three days on a sustainable farm service project, working alongside the local community. Through hands-on environmental stewardship, we gain a deeper appreciation for conservation and ethical travel practices.

Then we travel to the coast of Puntarenas for a kayaking expedition, exploring marine environments and camping beneath the stars. This phase of the program is all about teamwork, resilience and connection to nature.

weeks.title: Dolphins, surf & animal rescue
weeks.body:
Our kayaking expedition ends with a dolphin tour. Then we head to Jaco, where surf camp introduces us to Costa Rica’s Pacific waves, and a jungle walk and a zipline give new perspectives on the rainforest.

Next is the Costa Rica Animal Rescue Center in Turrucares, where after an orientation we start volunteering, supporting rehabilitation efforts and caring for animals such as sloths and monkeys.

weeks.title: Tortuguero, Pacuare rafting & farewell
weeks.location: Turrucares → Tortuguero → Pacuare River → San José
weeks.body:
A final day volunteering at the rescue center, then we explore Tortuguero National Park on a morning boat tour and spend a day volunteering in Tortuguero.

Our three-day rafting trip on the Pacuare River includes a hike to indigenous land and tree planting. Surrounded by rainforest and rushing water, we celebrate how far we’ve come as individuals and as a group. The program ends in San José, where we say our goodbyes before flying home.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: High activity level. Anyone with an average to advanced fitness level and an enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect multi-day hikes on Acatenango volcano and to Lake Atitlán, diving, kayaking, surfing, rafting and some physical work on volunteer projects.

items.title: Spanish through immersion
items.body: Lessons at Meztli Spanish School in Tulum and Sisai Language School in Quetzaltenango, practiced every day with your host family and on a language exchange with locals.

items.title: Marine conservation with Blue Ventures
items.body: Earn your PADI certification in Belize, then put it to use in conservation service learning on the Caribbean Sea.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: This is a high activity program suited to average to advanced fitness. You’ll need to be ready for multi-day hikes in Guatemala, including Acatenango volcano and Lake Atitlán, and some physical work on volunteer projects. You don’t need previous experience with any of the activities.

items.q: Do I need to know how to scuba dive?
items.a: No. You’ll learn from the beginning and work toward your PADI certification with Blue Ventures in Belize.

items.q: Do I need to speak Spanish?
items.a: No. Lessons at Meztli Spanish School in Tulum and Sisai Language School in Quetzaltenango are matched to your level, and you’ll practice with your host families.

Mostly clean, comfortable hostels and lodges, plus homestays with host families in Tulum and Quetzaltenango, camping on the sailing trip, volcano and lake hikes and the kayaking expedition, and the Doron Yoga & Zen Center.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
